parsed.explanation: The quote is verbatim and is indeed the whole contradiction step. The premise gives an infinite branch D_k with selected F_k disjoint from D_k, and one c in C lying in infinitely many F_k. Inserting c produces a DIFFERENT branch; what the text then shows (at best) is that on the modified branch the edge F_k is already met by c, so the element originally chosen from F_k need not be taken there. That is a statement about the modified branch, whereas the pruning rule forbids a contracted node on the branch under consideration. Nothing shows any x_j on the original infinite branch is dispensable, and 'dispensable' is never defined for a non-transversal partial label. So no contradiction with pruning is derived and the pruned tree is not shown finite. This is the only argument for finitely many minimal transversals, hence for B_1,...,B_s and L; obligation (F) fails.
